NEW DELHI: EPFO has asked its officers to aggressively contest adverse HC rulings in pension on higher wages (PoHW) cases under Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS), as the judgements have largely favoured pensioners and struck down the retirement savings body's circulars. To fight legal challenges arising from court rulings, field offices have been given standard defence templates and told to cite SC's Nov 2022 judgement in the Sunil Kumar case to secure division-bench stays against adverse single-judge orders and seek swift disposal, TOI has learnt. Central Board of Trustee is expected to discuss the matter Thursday. Under EPS, employee pension contributions and payouts were historically linked to the statutory wage cap regardless of actual earnings. At a monthly cap of Rs 15,000, 8.33% went towards EPS even if an employee earned Rs 1 lakh a month. Para 11(3) originally allowed employers and employees to jointly opt for contributions on actual salaries to secure a proportionately higher monthly pension. Govt deleted this provision in Aug 2014. In Nov 2022, SC upheld the 2014 amendments but gave eligible members in service on Sept 1, 2014, four months to apply for higher pensions. It excluded pre-2014 retirees who had missed the option. Nearly 99% of PoHW applications have been processed and settled, but about 2,800 cases remain in HCs. In many cases, EPFO remains in contempt for not complying with rulings. The disputes fall into several categories. Join conversation

 Although SC's 2022 ruling barred pre-2014 retirees who missed para 11(3) option from opting for PoHW, Kerala and Punjab & Haryana HCs granted relief. They ruled that a 2016 order continued to protect them and allowed people retiring after Sept 2014 to exercise the option. Another group of cases concerns exempted PF trusts, which manage employee funds under EPFO norms. Mostly public sector companies such as BHEL and NLC had capped contributions, but employees sought higher pensions after SC ruling. EPFO rejected the demand, but Madras and Calcutta HCs set aside its decision. In Sept, EPFO secured a stay on contempt proceedings.
